headline: High: gpt-engineer can write and execute code in a shared project directory, while Authelia can expose OAuth/OIDC auth flows and broad network egress, creating dangerous default interaction and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia can emit auth-related content via OIDC/ForwardAuth, and gpt-engineer reads/writes the project directory and stdin/stdout, so a manual or file-based bridge exists. However, no shared MCP or clipboard channel is documented, and Authelia is not shown ingesting gpt-engineer output by default.
conditions: IF Authelia output is copied into gpt-engineer prompts or files, prompt injection becomes plausible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same project directory, file-based instruction smuggling is possible.
mitigations: Keep Authelia-generated text out of gpt-engineer prompts.
Separate auth config files from prompt/input files.
Use a read-only handoff file for any shared text.
Review any copied output before pasting into gpt-engineer.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-engineer reads and writes the user project directory and sends content to a configured model, while Authelia has broad network egress and handles OAuth/OIDC flows. If sensitive project files or auth artifacts are shared, both agents can expose them through their respective network paths in default use.
conditions: IF the shared project directory contains secrets or auth configuration, gpt-engineer can read them.
IF Authelia is configured with real identity traffic, its network egress can carry sensitive auth metadata.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the shared project directory.
Store auth material in a separate vault or env file.
Run gpt-engineer on a scrubbed copy of the workspace.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce directory-level secret scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has write_filesystem and per-project shared state via the project directory, while Authelia is not runnable and exposes network/OIDC surfaces. The pair can still conflict over shared files or generated config artifacts even though Authelia itself lacks local write capability in the profile.
conditions: IF both agents target the same project directory, file overwrites can occur.
IF Authelia config is regenerated by gpt-engineer while another instance is active, state races are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Serialize edits to shared config files.
Use git branches or copies for generated changes.
Check for file diffs before applying output.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared project state.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files and can execute generated code with the user's privileges, so if Authelia-derived outputs are treated as authoritative inputs, errors can cascade into unsafe code or config changes. Authelia can produce auth-related outputs, and gpt-engineer's default workflow writes then offers to run, making the chain dangerous.
conditions: IF Authelia output is used as source material for generated code or config, downstream mistakes can be committed into files.
IF the user accepts gpt-engineer's offer to run generated code, bad outputs can execute with user privileges.
mitigations: Require human review before file writes are accepted.
Do not feed raw auth output into code generation.
Run generated code in a disposable sandbox first.
Diff generated files against a known-good baseline.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication system that can process identity data, while gpt-engineer handles project files and secrets such as OPENAI_API_KEY. Their default combination can mix auth data with code artifacts and logs, creating retention and residency mismatch risk even though no specific jurisdictional claim is documented.
conditions: IF identity data is stored in the same workspace as generated code, retention policies may diverge.
IF logs or artifacts are retained by both tools, deletion requests may not propagate consistently.
mitigations: Keep identity data out of the code workspace.
Separate logs by system and retention policy.
Document deletion/export handling for both tools.
Minimize stored auth traces.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls.
